How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MARCH 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-24 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for March 2024.

  D. FOURTH AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL AND MARK LAZZARETTO

  The proposed Fourth Amendment to the City Manager Employment
  Agreement would extend the City Manager’s term of employment by an
  additional five years, to February 5, 2031, and increase the City Manager’s base
  salary by five percent (5%), to $257,317. Additionally, the annual base salary of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 7, 2024  3
   the City Manager shall never be less than 105% of the top range of the base
  salary of the City’s next-highest paid employee. No change to any other
  provision of the employment agreement of any kind is proposed. The Fourth
  Amendment affirms an increase of $12,253 to the City Manager’s annual base
  salary. The annualized costs are covered in the existing 2024-2025 fiscal year
  budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Fourth Amendment to the
  City Manager Employment Agreement between the City of San Gabriel and
  Mark Lazzaretto.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 24-24 ADOPTING RETIREE MEDICAL VESTING UNDER
  SECTION 22904 OF THE PUBLIC EMPLOYES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL
  CARE ACT

  In November 2022, the City and its five distinct employee bargaining groups
  mutually agreed upon successor labor agreements. An important part of these
  agreements was the restructuring of the City’s retiree medical benefit provided
  by Section 22893 of the Public Employees’ Medical and Hospital Care Act
  (PEMHCA). Resolution No. 24-24 adopts Section 22904 of the Public
  Employees’ Medical and Hospital Care Act and establishes a multi-tiered retiree
  medical benefit system for the City of San Gabriel for employees starting service
  on January 1, 2023 and after. Resolution No. 24-24 and Section 22904 of
  PEMHCA are expected to markedly reduce the City’s $44.1 million Other Post
  Employment Benefits Liability over the next 10-15 years as the number of
  retiree medical beneficiaries subject to Section 22904 (Tier 3) increases.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-24, which
  approves the implementation of Section 22904 of Public Employees’ Medical
  and Hospital Care Act and establishes a third tier of retiree medical benefits for
  employees first hired on a full-time basis on or after January 1, 2023, and
  elected officials who first served as elected officials on or after January 1, 2023.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 7, 2024  4
   F. ORDINANCE NO. 706: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW FOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS AND
  JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (ZTA24-001) – SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 706 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning
  Code) of the San Gabriel Municipal Code (SGMC) relating to new state law for
  new accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units (ZTA24-001).
  Ordinance No. 706 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote at the City
  Council at the April 16, 2024, City Council meeting. The Fiscal Year 2023-24
  Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal publication and
  codification of the Ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines, the
  amendment to a Zoning Ordinance is not considered a project as defined in
  Section 15378 and can be seen with certainty that it will not have a significant
  effect on the environment. The proposed amendment to the Zoning Ordinance
  qualifies for this CEQA exemption as there is no possibility that the ordinance will
  have a significant effect on the environment as it amends the City’s Municipal
  Code to demonstrate compliance with State Accessory Dwelling Units Law.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  706 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA24-001, Amending Title XV,
  Chapter 153 (Zoning) Relating to New State Law for Accessory Dwelling Units
  and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units.”

  G. COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY FOR THE
  ANNUAL STREETS PROGRAM FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 AT AN ESTIMATED
  COST OF $557,015

  As part of this year’s Annual Streets Program, the City of San Gabriel plans to
  repave Broadway and Walnut Grove Avenue which are jurisdictionally shared
  between the City of San Gabriel and the County of Los Angeles. Due to the
  scope and cost of the project, the County policy requires a Cooperative
  Agreement be executed for the joint-agency repaving project. The City’s share
  is estimated to be $2,052,929.64 and the County’s share is estimated to be
  $557,015. The County will pay a deposit of $590,000 to the City, covering the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 7, 2024  5
   anticipated estimated project cost share of $557,015. Upon the completion of
  the project, the City will invoice the County for their actual share costs of the
  project.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorical Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – Existing
  Facilities. The project will improve the existing condition of local streets. No
  potential for significant impacts to the environment are anticipated in this project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Mayor of San Gabriel to
  execute the Cooperative Agreement between the City and Los Angeles County
  and authorize City staff to invoice Los Angeles County for their actual share
  costs of the project.

  H. APPROVAL OF L.A. METRO EXPRESSLANES NET TOLL REVENUE
  REINVESTMENT FUNDS AGREEMENT FOR THE SAN GABRIEL ROADWAY
  SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AND BIKE LANE INSTALLATION (CONTRACT NO.
  MX202304) FOR $1,269,109 AND APPROVAL OF THE CITY’S LABOR IN-
  KIND MATCH OF $162,600 WITH AN ADDITIONAL $80,000 OF MEASURE
  R MATCHING FUNDS TO ACQUIRE VIDEO DETECTION SYSTEMS

  The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
  awarded the San Gabriel Roadway Safety Improvements and Bike Lane
  Installation Project with a total project budget of $1,511,709. This project aims
  to improve bike and pedestrian safety at 13 locations, extend the bike lane on
  Del Mar Avenue to bridge the gap leading to the City of San Marino, and install
  25 Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB) at 25 existing high-risk crosswalk
  locations. The City is required to enter into funding agreements with LACMTA
  to accept $1,269,109 of Net Toll Revenue Reinvestment Funds. The project
  requires the City to provide $162,600 labor in-kind match, along with $80,000
  of Measure R Matching funds.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This is not a project
  as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines. The project will include
  the improvement of the existing intersections and addition of additional striping
  and markings to the existing roadways within the public right-of-way facility.
  Irrespective of the exemption, no potential significant impacts to the environment
  are anticipated from this project.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 7, 2024  6
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority Funding Agreement MXL Grant
  #MX202304 in Toll Revenue Reinvestment funds for the San Gabriel Roadway
  Safety Improvements and Bike Lane Installation Project, authorize the Mayor to
  execute the funding agreements on behalf of the City, and approve the City’s
  labor in-kind match of $162,600 with an additional $80,000 of Measure R
  Matching funds to acquire video detection systems as part of Capital
  Improvement Project #2-21-02.

  I. MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS APPROVING A PROPORTIONAL SHARE OF
  THE ADDITIONAL EXPENDITURES RELATED TO THE 2018-2023
  MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $8,599.32 FOR
  VARIOUS STORMWATER MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS [RESOLUTION NO.
  24-23]

  The 2018-2023 Memorandum of Agreement between the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Government (SGVCOG) and the City, intended for administration and
  cost sharing in the implementation of monitoring programs, exceeded the
  original scope of work. The City’s proportional overage share is $8,599.32. In
  order to reconcile these overages, the SCVCOG will enter into a new agreement
  with the City to facilitate payment collection.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-23 to
  appropriate $8,599.32 from the Safe, Clean Water Program (Measure W) fund
  to the Stormwater Contractual account 138-800-03-22-000, authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Memorandum of Agreement with the San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments, and approve a purchase order in the amount
  of $8,599.32 using account number 138-800-03-22-000.

  J. APPROVAL OF MISSION PLAYHOUSE TICKETING SOFTWARE CONTRACT
  WITH AUDIENCEVIEW

  Since 2016, the City of San Gabriel has used Ticketmaster LLC for ticketing
  services for the Mission Playhouse. The initial User Agreement had a set term
  of three years and expired in December of 2019.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 7, 2024  7
   Staff has reviewed options for new ticketing software and recommends the
  approval of a contract with AudienceView. The proposed agreement is for five
  years and will be up for renewal in April of 2029.

  The report recommends the City Council discontinue the partnership with
  Ticketmaster and authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with
  AudienceView.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the AudienceView contract
  effective immediately and include the related ongoing expenses in the Fiscal
  Year 2024-25 budget. Staff also recommends that the City Council authorize
  the City Manager to execute the contract with Card Connect pending approval
  by the City Attorney.

  K. PURCHASE OF NEW POLICE MOTORCYCLE - $39,316.78

  Public Works Fleet staff have determined that the 2015 Honda police
  motorcycle is long overdue for replacement as a viable patrol motorcycle and
  will likely soon need major repairs. The proposed replacement for the 2015
  Honda ST 1300 is the 2024 Harley Davidson FLTRXP which is more reliable, has
  lower maintenance costs, and has been a tested and proven a more reliable
  police motorcycle than the older Honda which has been phased out of service
  at many agencies.  Honda has discontinued its production of police
  motorcycles. This information was confirmed by the 48th Annual Law
  Enforcement Motorcycle Test and Evaluation program conducted in 2022. The
  Harley Davidson model received the overall rating of “Above Average” for the
  evaluation, and no major manufacturer changes have been implemented in
  2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the purchase of one 2024
  Harley Davidson from Laidlaw Harley Davidson utilizing Office of Traffic Safety
  Selective Traffic Enforcement Program Grant #24174 funds from account #124-
  751-52-99-201.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 7, 2024  8
  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PROPOSED CITYWIDE FEE SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025
  [RESOLUTION NO. 24-26]

  The citywide fee schedule establishes user fees and charges for various
  department-related services. User fees and regulatory fees charged by the City
  may not exceed the estimated reasonable cost to provide the service or
  regulate the activity. Fees for the use of public property are considered rents.
  Rents are set at the discretion of the City and are not limited by cost recovery.
  The consumer price index (CPI) for the Los Angeles Metro area, for January
  2024, increased by 2.5%. Based on the Fiscal Year 2024-25 forecasted revenues,
  a 2.5% to general fund fees is estimated to generate approximately an
  additional $160,000 in general fund revenue.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-26 updating
  the Master Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2024-25.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.
